chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Baḥr, from Kirdīn al-Mismaʿī, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام saying: A man should not dye himself while he is in a state of janabah, nor should he perform ghusl while he is dyed.

key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.مُخْتَضِبٌ: being in a state of having applied dye
key_terms.يَخْتَضِبُ: applies dye, such as henna or similar coloring

ai.seo_question: Can a person in janabah apply dye or perform ghusl while dyed?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling concerning ritual purity and the etiquette of using dye. It states that a person in janabah should not apply dye, and that one should not perform ghusl while already dyed, indicating an order and propriety in matters of taharah.
